item.title: Mad Skillz Puts Richmond Teens First With Holiday Gift Drive
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mad Skillz joins Richmond's Art Bus gift drive, where books, headphones and sports gear can help make a teen's holiday.
item.content:encoded:
Mad Skillz is teaming up with Richmond’s transit agency to collect holiday gifts for local kids, with a special push to reach teenagers.

The rapper will help kick off “Santa’s Got Skillz” at the Richmond Christmas Parade on December 5, where he’ll ride with Greater Richmond Transit Company employees as the agency’s Art Bus follows.

The plan is to fill the bus with new, unwrapped gifts and get them to families through four local nonprofits, GRTC announced.

Those partners are ASK Childhood Cancer Foundation, Peter Paul Development Center, Ronald McDonald House Charities of Richmond and Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Richmond.

The drive especially wants gifts for ages 13 to 17, including headphones, art supplies, sports gear or games. The Art Bus will start taking donations after the parade and make more stops December 9 through 12.

“Thank you to Mad Skillz for inspiring us to do big things right here in our community, where it matters most,” Richmond Mayor Danny Avula said.

The agency said the Boys & Girls Club was among the groups that helped inspire him.

In August, Skillz offered to buy school shoes for kids he met shopping with their families at Richmond-area malls. He told parents he tries to do it every year before classes start, and said he helped 13 families on the first day.

Richmond has been part of his work for decades.

He started rapping on the University of Richmond’s radio station and returned as an artist-in-residence to help teach a course on Hip-Hop.

He told AllHipHop about fighting for a place for Virginia in rap before his spoken-word records earned him Grammys.

“From the time I started rapping and taking music seriously all I knew was that I was proud of where I was from,” Skillz said.

His first Grammy came this year for Words For Days Vol. 1, which featured 14 Richmond-area collaborators.

The Recording Academy has since nominated him in the same spoken-word poetry album category for A Hero And A Villain, his third straight nomination.

After the parade, the first collection stop is the Willow Lawn Target at 5401 West Broad Street from 1 to 3 P.M.

item.title: Nelly Moves Black And White Ball To Bigger Venue For Its 15th Edition
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nelly's Black and White Ball moves to St. Charles for its 15th edition, supporting Make-A-Wish Missouri and college scholarships.
item.content:encoded:
Nelly is moving his Black and White Ball out of downtown St. Louis for its 15th edition. Organizers announced that the December 13 fundraiser will take place at Ameristar Casino Resort Spa in St. Charles, Missouri, instead of the Four Seasons, FOX 2 St. Louis reported.

Nelly said the extra room came from a bigger commitment from sponsors this year.

“The Black and White Ball has always been about giving back to our city’s youth and celebrating our love for St. Louis,” he said in the announcement.

The money raised at the gala will help Make-A-Wish Missouri grant wishes to children with critical illnesses.

The event will also fund college scholarships for St. Louis students attending Harris-Stowe State University, the city’s historically Black university.

The scholarship tie goes back years. Nelly hosted the first ball in 2006 and kept it going annually through 2016.

When he brought the fundraiser back in 2023, scholarships for local students and support for Make-A-Wish remained part of the program.

Students received scholarships at the Four Seasons last December, when Olympic gold medalist Jackie Joyner-Kersee received the ball’s Legend Award.

Nelly also used the night to grant a child’s wish for a family trip to Disney World.

Past editions have drawn artists including Ashanti, Janet Jackson, Busta Rhymes, Monica and Boyz II Men, alongside St. Louis sports figures. Cardinals Hall of Famer Ozzie Smith received the first Legend Award after the gala returned in 2023.

Nelly spoke about giving computers, bicycles and scholarships to kids in an earlier interview with AllHipHop.

The St. Louis rapper tied that work to a belief that his hometown should see some of the benefits of his career, alongside his plans for business in the city.

Derrty Entertainment and Synergy Productions are producing the event, with the Daugherty Foundation as title sponsor. The foundation is among the groups helping put the gala in a larger room. The new venue still puts the event in the St. Louis region, across the Missouri River from St. Louis County.

The organizers’ announcement named past guests but did not name this year’s performers or list ticket prices.

item.title: Mannie Fresh, Juvenile & T.I. Bring Their Southern Rap History To Jazz Fest
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mannie Fresh, Juvenile and T.I. share a 2027 Jazz Fest billing, with LL Cool J, Wyclef Jean and Big Freedia on weekend two.
item.content:encoded:
Mannie Fresh is bringing Juvenile and T.I. to New Orleans Jazz Fest under one billing.

The festival announced its 2027 lineup Thursday (November 19), placing the trio on the second weekend alongside LL Cool J, Wyclef Jean and Big Freedia.

Mannie and Juvenile have spent much of this fall on the same bill. Both were part of the Cash Money & No Limit Tour, the arena run led by Birdman and Master P that included a September stop at New Orleans’ Smoothie King Center.

The new festival date pairs them with an Atlanta rapper whose own work with Mannie stretches back two decades.

Mannie produced T.I.’s “Top Back” for his 2006 album King.

In an interview with Splice, he recalled trying to get T.I. signed to Cash Money years earlier and said the record started with Juvenile: “And the crazy thing is, ‘Top Back’ was actually Juvie’s song.”

Fresh added, “And I had Tip do the hook before Juvie walked into the studio.”

All three revisited how the beat changed hands on Mannie and Juvenile’s Still 400 podcast.

Before that, Mannie had helped turn Juvenile’s New Orleans club records into national hits.

He produced “Back That Azz Up” and changed the drums on “Ha,” a song Juvenile was already taking to local crowds before recording 400 Degreez.

The two have kept finding new ways to play those records. For Juvenile’s Tiny Desk concert, Mannie worked alongside the 400 Degreez Band, with New Orleans musicians Trombone Shorty and Jon Batiste joining the set.

The second weekend runs April 29 through May 2 at the Fair Grounds Race Course.

LL Cool J is billed with DJ Z-Trip and Technician The DJ, while Chaka Khan is booked for the opening weekend, April 22 through 25. New Orleans acts on the second weekend also include Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue, the Soul Rebels and Rebirth Brass Band.

item.title: Jazzy Jay’s NYC Birthday Brings Out DJ Premier, Red Alert & Hip-Hop Pioneers
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: DJ Premier, Kool DJ Red Alert, Crazy Legs and Melle Mel celebrated Jazzy Jay, whose records helped get Def Jam started.
item.content:encoded:
Jazzy Jay marked his birthday with a Hip-Hop History Month gathering in New York. DJ Premier, Kool DJ Red Alert, Crazy Legs and Melle Mel gathered Wednesday (November 18) at Hidden Tiger at Fat Social Club in the East Village.

The lineup brought together DJs, breakers and MCs.

Crazy Legs came out of the Rock Steady Crew’s breaking scene, Melle Mel was an MC in Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, and Premier took his production from Gang Starr to records with artists such as Nas.

For Red Alert and Jazzy Jay, the connection goes back to family and two turntables.

Red Alert recalled teaching his cousin the basics before Jay started getting work in the Bronx.

Jay played on Disco King Mario’s sound system and later helped bring Red Alert into the Zulu Nation’s circle.

“Jazzy kept talking to him about me, ‘Put my cousin down,'” Red Alert recalled of Afrika Bambaataa.

Jazzy Jay used another sound system, the one he’d built into his Chevy Caprice, when he and Rick Rubin were working on “It’s Yours” with T La Rock.

He told AllHipHop they’d test mixes in the car and go back upstairs if the bass wasn’t right.

“We’d park, pump the sounds, and sell twelve-inches. That was the beginning days of Def Jam.”

Cornell University Library’s original 12-inch shows both the Partytime and Def Jam catalog numbers.

The archive makes a distinction: “It’s Yours” carried the Def Jam name before Rubin and Russell Simmons put out their first record as a team, LL Cool J’s “I Need a Beat.”

Jazzy Jay also recorded “Def Jam,” backed with “Cold Chillin’ in the Spot,” with Simmons on the flip side. The 1985 release put Jay’s scratching and electronically altered voice on the title track.

item.title: FullyGangJit Dies At 25, A Day Before New Single Arrives
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: FullyGangJit, a 25-year-old Baton Rouge rapper, dies in a shooting one day before his collaboration with Bty Beedo arrives.
item.content:encoded:
FullyGangJit, an independent Baton Rouge rapper who put out a series of projects through 25/7 Records, was shot and killed in his home city on November 17.

He was 25. A collaboration with Bty Beedo arrived on streaming services a day after his death.

Baton Rouge police identified the rapper as Micah Farlough and said the shooting happened around 12:47 A.M. at a market at 3916 Plank Road, WBRZ reported.

Farlough was taken to a hospital, where he died. The East Baton Rouge Parish Coroner’s Office said it received a call from the hospital around 2:50 a.m.

Detectives had not named a suspect or identified a motive when they released Farlough’s name.

FullyGangJit had spent the past few years building a catalog with collaborators from the local scene.

In an interview with SquadTV, he discussed his move from athletics to music, how he picked his stage name and what it took to keep putting out records on his own. The conversation also covered how he developed his sound in Baton Rouge.

Among his earlier recordings was a 2023 appearance on BWay Never Broke Again’s “Me vs Me, Pt. 2,” a group track that also features Mg Woodie, Monewaypeso and Stacks Osama.

By 2025, he was releasing projects under his own name, including FullyVille, FullyVille2 and Still Bleeding. Monewaypeso returned for “DSG Shit” on FullyVille and “Confirm The Kill” on the sequel.

The artist’s streaming catalog shows his releases continued this year with Product Of The Trenches.

He released a deluxe edition on August 7, bringing the album to 19 songs. Longtime collaborator Tmh Joker appeared on the album cut “Pick Em Up” and had already worked with him on “Triple Threat.”

The record released after his death was “Buss It Baby,” the November 18 single credited to FullyGangJit and Bty Beedo on the same label.

Baton Rouge police asked anyone with information about the shooting to call the Capital Region Crime Stoppers tip line at (225) 344-7867.

item.title: The Alchemist Opens His Hip-Hop Archive Inside A Giant Sampler
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The Alchemist's museum tour reveals a giant MPC, an Action Bronson rhyme on a phone bill and three decades of rap history.
item.content:encoded:
The Alchemist built his pop-up museum around a version of the Akai MPC 2500 big enough for fans to walk inside.

In a new walkthrough for FRANK151, the producer revisited how he met Erykah Badu and recalled Action Bronson writing a rhyme on his phone bill.

The tour takes viewers back to the first Alchemist Museum of Sound, which ran November 14 and 15 at Camp Flog Gnaw in Los Angeles.

The festival placed it in Okaga Village, where fans could see photos, videos and material the producer saved from recording sessions, tours and album shoots. The temporary exhibit covered three decades of his work.

“If you know me you know i save everything,” The Alchemist wrote in his announcement.

The oversized MPC was the walk-in centerpiece, but visitors could also tap pads on a sampler. The producer said they could “hear the actual sounds from some of your favorite beats.”

That model wasn’t just a prop picked for its shape.

The producer used his MPC 2500 to chop the sample and program drums for ScHoolboy Q’s “Kno Ya Wrong,” a process he breaks down in his Aulart class. The 2500 and the Renaissance are among the samplers he prefers for their hands-on controls.

The Bronson story goes back to a partnership that yielded the 2012 mixtape Rare Chandeliers and the seven-track Lamb Over Rice in 2019.

His partnership with Badu shows another way the machine brought people together.

She worked out her own take on his drum machine before hearing his version of “Hot BiBi (Apostle 2),” and they combined their ideas for Before The World Blows, their joint album released in August.

The pair had already tried out the material at small, phone-free shows, with The Alchemist on the MPC, according to their album announcement.

The Alchemist also put together a limited museum EP with music from Prodigy, Larry June and 2 Chainz, plus Earl Sweatshirt and Boldy James.

Alongside the samplers, the festival listed floppy disks, handwritten lyrics and film photographs among the objects on display.

item.title: Lloyd Banks & DJ Whoo Kid Revive “Mo Money In The Bank” After Nearly 20 Years
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lloyd Banks and DJ Whoo Kid are reviving their Mo Money In The Bank mixtape series nearly 20 years after The Final Chapter.
item.content:encoded:
Lloyd Banks is reopening the Mo Money In The Bank mixtape series he and DJ Whoo Kid closed out in 2006 with a tape called The Final Chapter.

The Queens rapper and his longtime DJ released a joint Instagram teaser Thursday, and the nearly two-minute video revisits the artwork from earlier installments, including the first tape, Cashing In and the fifth volume’s Rotten Apple design.

“Once again It’s On!!!!!!!!!!!!” Banks wrote in the caption, tagging Whoo Kid. The teaser does not give a full mixtape release date or track list.

There is, separately, a new Banks single named “Money In The Bank,” but that is a song, not a confirmed date for the sixth tape.

The pairing goes back to the G-Unit run, when Banks released street tapes alongside his major-label albums.

Mo Money In The Bank, Pt. 5 (The Final Chapter) dropped in December 2006, with both Banks and Whoo Kid credited on the opener.

That was the year Banks put out his second solo album, Rotten Apple.

The fourth tape appeared before that album, giving the rapper another outlet while the commercial release moved through two date changes.

When Banks spoke to AllHipHop about that era, he described a choice between addressing a rival on a national release and keeping the response on a mixtape.

His goal was to bring that same direct style to records people heard on the radio.

In another AllHipHop interview, Banks recalled not knowing what would happen when he, Tony Yayo and 50 Cent first put out 50 Cent Is The Future.

“We made a mixtape in a matter of two days. 8 records a day type sh*t,” Banks said.

He has gone back to a familiar series before. Whoo Kid worked with him on his first Halloween Havoc tape in 2008, giving the two another series beyond Mo Money In The Bank.

Banks released the sixth Halloween Havoc on October 31, 2025.

item.title: Odd Future’s Left Brain Proposes To Melanie Bickel Onstage At Camp Flog Gnaw
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Left Brain proposed to longtime girlfriend Melanie Bickel during his Camp Flog Gnaw set, then returned as a guest the next day.
item.content:encoded:
Left Brain asked a question at Camp Flog Gnaw that had nothing to do with his set list.

The Odd Future rapper and producer proposed to his longtime girlfriend, Melanie Bickel, during his performance at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles on November 14.

She said yes.

TITI Atelier, the jeweler that made the ring, said Left Brain got down on one knee and that the couple cried after Bickel accepted. The ring has a yellow center stone and a hidden lovebird inspired by their shared affection for Tweety Bird.

The proposal happened at a festival started by his Odd Future collaborator Tyler, The Creator.

Left Brain had his own booking on the sold-out weekend, and he returned to the stage in a familiar role the next day. The Daily Trojan reported that Mike G brought him and Casey Veggies out during a separate Sunday set.

Left Brain was part of Odd Future from its early Los Angeles days. He and Hodgy Beats formed MellowHype and put out YelloWhite and BlackenedWhite as free downloads through Odd Future’s site in 2010.

Fat Possum reissued BlackenedWhite the next year, taking the duo’s music from the collective’s website to stores.

He also produced “Rella,” the song that put Hodgy, Domo Genesis and Tyler on the same record when the group rolled out The O.F. Tape Vol. 2 in 2012.

His later Mind Gone projects put him on the mic, too. In an interview with StockX, he said he got tired of sending out beats and waiting for other people to release them.

“Rap a little bit because producing can get a little boring for me,” he said. “I wanna put shit out, so I’m gonna use my voice.”

During his own set, Left Brain brought a live saxophone and trumpet to the Gnaw Stage and played a new track, “Engage,” and a cover of Rage Against the Machine’s “Killing in the Name,” according to mxdwn’s review.

The review also reported that fans could find a coffee stand called Left Brain Lattes away from the stage.

He waited until the end of his set to ask Bickel to marry him, as i-D reported from the festival.

item.title: Lil Durk’s Lawyer Plans Double Jeopardy Fight Over Remaining Charges
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Drew Findling says Lil Durk's defense will use his murder-for-hire acquittal to challenge a second federal trial.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Durk’s lawyer says the defense will argue that the rapper’s acquittal should stop federal prosecutors from trying him on the charges he still faces.

Drew Findling laid out the double jeopardy argument in an interview on The Breakfast Club.

“One of our constitutional rights is double jeopardy. You can’t be tried for the same thing twice,” Findling said.

He said the Los Angeles shooting remains at the center of the government’s case, even though prosecutors are pursuing different counts.

A federal jury acquitted Durk in the murder-for-hire prosecution on all five counts on September 11.

Prosecutors alleged he backed a 2022 attack near the Beverly Center that targeted rapper Quando Rondo. Rondo survived, but his cousin Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson was killed.

The verdict did not end the case. Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald had split the later racketeering and gun charges from the murder-for-hire trial after prosecutors added allegations tied to a 2022 killing in Chicago and a 2019 shooting in Atlanta.

The defense had already prepared for the Los Angeles trial and objected to adding the new allegations so close to jury selection. Fitzgerald let the original trial go first.

Findling said he expects prosecutors to connect those other incidents to the Los Angeles shooting.

He pointed out that Durk wasn’t charged in the original Chicago prosecution and that the Georgia case was dismissed.

The Chicago allegations center on the death of Stephon Mack outside a community center. He said the defense would argue that the first jury has already decided the central issue.

“We will definitely be battling it out,” Findling said.

Prosecutors already argued in their opposition to bond that the acquittal did not resolve the broader allegations. Durk has pleaded not guilty to the remaining charges.

The dispute over a second trial is separate from Durk’s request to go home while he waits. Fitzgerald heard arguments on November 4 and took the bond request under submission.

Durk’s lawyers offered future music income and other money and property to secure his return to court.

Durk remains in custody, and his second trial is set for August 30, 2027.

item.title: Boosie Badazz Avoids Indictment In Houston Nightclub Case
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: A Houston grand jury declined to indict Boosie Badazz over a May nightclub confrontation. A separate civil suit remains.
item.content:encoded:
Boosie Badazz will not stand trial on the Houston nightclub assault charge after a Harris County grand jury declined to indict him on Friday, November 20, his lawyer Kent Schaffer told TMZ.

Schaffer said the aggravated assault case was dismissed after the grand jury returned a no-bill. Under Texas law, at least nine grand jurors have to vote to indict. A no-bill means the case did not get enough votes to go to trial.

Schaffer said the defense had believed from the start that the case was financially motivated. He told TMZ that “the grand jury agreed that there was no probable cause to believe a crime was committed.”

The case stemmed from a May 24 incident at Dome Nightclub in downtown Houston, where Boosie had been booked over Memorial Day weekend. A security guard said he was escorting a woman out at closing time when he was struck with a glass hookah base.

The guard told investigators that he saw Boosie holding the broken base when he turned around. A second guard told police he heard glass break and saw Boosie holding pieces of it, according to court records reviewed by Houston’s KPRC. Both guards identified the rapper to investigators by his stage name.

Boosie appeared in court June 1 and had his bond set at $85,000. His attorney at that hearing, Carl A. Moore, told FOX 26 Houston that the rapper was defending another person during the confrontation.

Boosie addressed the accusation himself after that court appearance. “The facts of the case will come out,” he said in a Facebook video reported by WBRZ, and disputed the guard’s version of what happened.

The case was still active in September, when Boosie returned to a Harris County courtroom. The case against the Baton Rouge rapper centered on the allegation that the hookah base had been used as a deadly weapon.

The criminal outcome doesn’t settle the separate civil suit brought by the security guard, Edward Iglehart II. He alleges assault and battery over what happened at the club and defamation over remarks Boosie made afterward.

Iglehart is seeking $8 million in damages, as AllHipHop previously reported.
